summary:
Read-only audit of src/sim/h2rSound.js (203 lines), src/sim/gt3Sound.js (225), src/sim/sound.js (298) and their callers (h2rRide.js:330, gt3Drive.js:562, main.js:616/1631). I took the two AudioWorklet DSP strings out of the files and ran them offline in Node at 48 kHz, using scratch harnesses in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-spacex/49448258-b837-551e-9b35-7fac201f56d4/scratchpad/diag/ (run.mjs, analyse.mjs, variants.mjs, chirp.mjs, clicks.mjs, level.mjs). Nothing in the repo was edited.

What the engines already do well: both are built from exhaust pulses timed by the real crank angle (firing order, cylinder-to-cylinder spread, overrun pops, limiter and shift cuts). So the order content follows physics. Measured relative to the firing order:
- H2R (inline four): order 2 dominates, order 4 sits at -1 to -8 dB, half orders at -26 to -50 dB.
- GT3 (flat six): order 3 dominates, order 6 at -5 to -19 dB, order 1.5 at -7 to -29 dB.

What makes them sound synthetic, in order of impact:
1. **Firing times rounded to whole samples.** Each firing lands on the nearest sample. When the firing period is not a whole number of samples, this adds an rpm-dependent noise floor. Measured with randomness switched off: -25 dB at 14,000 rpm (H2R) and -27 dB at 8,900 rpm (GT3), against -48 to -54 dB at rpms where the period is a whole number. Placing each firing at its exact fractional time (tested) brings it down to -42 to -49 dB, a 15–19 dB gain. This is the 'digital grit' heard on rev sweeps. Aliasing from tanh is small by comparison (about -44 to -48 dB).
2. **The H2R relief-valve chirp is broken.** Its phase is computed as sc*(0.6+chirp), and sc runs freely up to 1e6 rad. After about 30 s of riding, every chirp comes out at random frequencies between 2 and 47 kHz (aliased noise). It is also never triggered on quick-shift upshifts, because the sound reads the rider's throttle (which stays open), not the engine's.
3. **Nothing depends on where the camera is.** Both cars feed one mono signal straight to the output, so trackside, chase, orbit and onboard all sound alike. There is no propagation delay, Doppler, distance loss, panning, air absorption, ground reflection or reverb. A trackside pass-by at 250 km/h should drop about 7 semitones (factor 1.25 → 0.83) and swell about +19 dB. The H2R is not even told which camera is active.
4. **Parameter changes step and click.** Controls arrive by postMessage once per frame and are smoothed once per 128-sample block, so pitch changes in stair-steps that depend on frame rate. The on/off flag cuts instantly: an H2R crash makes a 0.77 sample-to-sample jump, against 0.23 in normal running.
5. **Timbre does not track rpm and load well.** The pulse shape is a fixed 1–2.5 ms exponential instead of following crank angle. Level and brightness are flattened by a per-sample tanh with an rpm term, followed by a compressor: the A-weighted level rises only about 10 dB from 3,000 to 14,000 rpm (H2R) and about 11 dB from 2,000 to 9,000 (GT3). The exhaust is four or five fixed parallel band-pass filters rather than a model of the pipe, so there is no pipe-mode comb and no tuning that follows gas temperature.
6. **Supercharger whine is at the wrong order.** The H2R whine is synthesised at 9.2× crank, which is the shaft's own rotation. Kawasaki publishes a 69 mm impeller with 6 blades at the tip and 12 at the base, so the blade-pass tones fall at 55.2× and 110.4× crank: about 12.9 kHz and 25.8 kHz at 14,000 rpm. The second is above Nyquist and must not be synthesised.
7. **Volume balance against wind is off.** Wind gain scales with speed², which is 40 dB per decade. The SWOV helmet data (94 → 106 dB from 100 → 160 km/h) works out to about 59 dB per decade, i.e. speed³. At 200 km/h the H2R wind (RMS 0.042) sits about 18 dB under the engine (about 0.34), where in reality it would roughly match or cover it.
8. **Smaller issues.**
   - Both worklets leave a DC offset of about 0.03, because the DC blocker sits before the last nonlinearity.
   - The GT3 PDK downshift blip and upshift crack are mostly inaudible, because the sound gets the input throttle rather than the engine throttle and no pop is injected on a shift.
   - The valve-train 'tick' is a pure tone at order 12, not a train of clicks.
   - Tyre squeal frequency is re-randomised every frame.
   - Three separate AudioContexts, each with its own compressor.

Rocket (sound.js) is the most physical of the three: retarded time, HRTF panning, ground-reflection comb, convolution reverb, N-wave booms. Still missing or off:
- No Doppler, although the retarded-time slope dτ/dt is exactly the Doppler factor and is already computed implicitly. About ×0.41 for a booster leaving at 500 m/s.
- Air absorption is about 4× too bright at every distance compared with the ISO 9613 coefficients (cutoff 15000·250/d against a measured 3 dB point of about 2.5 kHz at 250 m, about 900 Hz at 1 km, about 110 Hz at 10 km).
- The reverb impulse response is cut off abruptly at -34 dB, at 3.6 s.
- The 'roar' band peaks at 160 Hz, whereas measured super-heavy launch sound power peaks at 10–20 Hz (Kellison & Gee 2023, SLS at 1.4–1.8 km).

CPU: each worklet costs about 0.8% of one core, so there is roughly 10× headroom for fractional delays, pipe models, oversampling and an order layer.

Published facts used versus estimates:
- PUBLISHED: H2R impeller 9.2× crank, about 130,000 /min, 6 blades at the tip and 12 at the base (Kawasaki press kit). 992 GT3 individual throttle bodies and two resonance flaps (Porsche press kit, via search snippet). 9,000 /min redline. GT3 final drive 4.27 and H2R primary 76/49, final 42/18 (repo data). Helmet wind levels (SWOV). SLS sound-power peak 10–20 Hz (JASA Express Letters 3, 113601). Starship IFT-5 at about 10 km: 105–125 dB, boom at the catch the loudest event (Gee et al. 2024, JASA Express Letters, via press coverage).
- NOT FOUND: no published order spectrum for the 992 GT3 RS or the H2R. Order 3 (flat six) and order 2 (even-firing inline four) follow from engine physics; every relative order level, pipe length and pulse shape below is an approximation to be marked ≈ in code and README, per CLAUDE.md.

Sources: [roadracingworld H2R press info](https://roadracingworld.com/?p=20812), [Kawasaki H2 press kit PDF](https://asset.moto.it/pricelist/moto/af2988c76bda4343bcfbc4cab4afc019/presskit-kawasaki-h2-2015.pdf), [Porsche 911 GT3 media kit](https://media.porsche.com/mediakit/911-gt3/en/the-new-911-gt3/engine-and-transmission) (403 on fetch; only the search snippet was used), [Kellison & Gee 2023 via NSF PAR](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10500729), [Smithsonian on the BYU Starship study](https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/heres-what-a-spacex-starship-rocket-launch-sounds-like-according-to-new-detailed-data-180985498/), [NSF on Starship's sound study](https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2024/11/starships-sound-study1/), [SWOV wind noise in motorcycle helmets](https://swov.nl/en/publicatie/wind-noise-motorcycle-helmets), [xbhp on the H2 relief-valve chirp](https://www.xbhp.com/?p=42465), [EP2933471 Kawasaki relief-valve patent](https://data.epo.org/publication-server/rest/v1.2/patents/EP2933471NWA1/document.html), [SAE 910619 order-based exhaust synthesis](https://saemobilus.sae.org/content/910619/).

findings.title: Firing impulses rounded to whole samples: rpm-dependent inharmonic noise floor (main source of 'digital grit')
findings.evidence: h2rSound.js:61-71 and gt3Sound.js:81-93 add the whole pulse amplitude to the sample where theta crosses next (`imp += a`; `impA/impB += a`). Offline test at 48 kHz with randomness and noise layers off (variants.mjs): inharmonic energy is -25.2 dB at H2R 14,000 rpm and -32.5 dB / -27.4 dB at GT3 7,000 / 8,900 rpm, against -48 to -54 dB at rpms where the period is a whole number of samples (H2R 6,000 and 10,000; GT3 4,000). Splitting each impulse across two samples by its sub-sample position gives -43.9 dB (H2R 14k), -48.8 dB (GT3 7k) and -42.2 dB (GT3 8.9k). Rendering at 192 kHz gives about the same as the fractional version (-42.9 dB), so tanh aliasing is not the main issue.
findings.fix: Carry a fractional remainder. H2R (same pattern for GT3 with this.cA/this.cB per bank and 2π/3 spacing): `let imp = this.carry; this.carry = 0; while (this.theta >= this.next) { const fr = (this.theta - this.next) / dTheta; this.next += Math.PI; ...compute a...; imp += a * fr; this.carry += a * (1 - fr); }`. Initialise `this.carry = 0` (GT3: `this.cA = this.cB = 0`) in the constructor. This adds one sample of latency, which is irrelevant. Better still: band-limited impulses (4-point Lagrange or a polyBLEP-style 4-tap kernel) spread over 4 samples.

findings.title: H2R relief-valve chirp is aliased noise after ~30 s, and never fires on quick-shifts
findings.evidence: h2rSound.js:102 computes `Math.sin(this.sc * (0.6 + this.chirp))`. sc is a free-running phase that wraps only at 1e6 rad (line 95), so the instantaneous frequency includes sc·Δchirp. chirp.mjs: with sc=10 at trigger the chirp runs 1637→781→952 Hz (falls, then rises again); with sc=3e5 or 9e5 (reached after about 30 s at 11,000 rpm) the per-25 ms frequency jumps between 2.5 and 47 kHz, i.e. aliased garbage. The intended sweep is 2699 → 1012 Hz. The trigger (line 51) needs this.thr to drop from above 0.6 to below 0.2, but h2rSound.update passes i.throttle (line 183), which stays at 1 during a quick-shift; h2rBike.js:147 zeroes only the engine's internal thr. Recordings show a squeak at every shift (xbhp; Kawasaki relief-valve patent EP2933471).
findings.fix: Give the chirp its own phase accumulator: `this.chPh += 2*Math.PI*fCh/sr; if (this.chPh > 2*Math.PI) this.chPh -= 2*Math.PI; y += (Math.sin(this.chPh)*0.6 + bandNoise*0.4) * this.chirp * 0.15;` with `fCh = (2200 + 1800*this.chirp) * Math.sqrt(boostAtTrigger)` (≈, by ear) and a decay of about 60 ms. Trigger on (a) the rising edge of the new message field `shift` while load > 0.5 and rpm > 7000, and (b) the engine throttle closing on boost. Send `shift: s.shift > 0 ? 1 : 0` and `engThr` (see the load finding) from update(). Add a band-noise 'pssh' (band-pass about 3–5 kHz) under the tone, since a relief valve is mostly flow noise.

findings.title: No spatial model for the car and bike sounds: no delay, Doppler, distance, panning, air absorption, ground reflection or reverb; H2R ignores the camera completely
findings.evidence: Both build() functions run engine → (cabinLp) → master → compressor → destination, in mono (outputChannelCount [1]). gt3Drive.js:562 passes only `state.camera === 'driver'`; h2rRide.js:330 passes no camera information at all. The trackside camera (gt3Drive.js:346-356, h2rRide.js:135-145) sits 45+1.2u m ahead and 14 m to the side. At u=69 m/s that is 128 m → 14 m: Doppler 343/(343-69·0.994)=1.25 approaching and 0.83 receding (a 1.50 ratio, about 7 semitones), with a +19 dB swell from 1/r. The ground-reflection notch sweeps from about 17 kHz to 1.6 kHz (exhaust h≈0.4 m, ear 1.6 m). None of this is heard. sound.js:247-253 already implements the reflection and absorption maths for the rocket.
findings.fix: Create src/sim/audioSpace.js (shared). `createEmitter(ctx, {maxDelay:1.5})` returns input → DelayNode (propagation and Doppler) → air BiquadFilter (lowpass) plus a second DelayNode/gain for the ground reflection (copy sound.js:132-135/247-251) → PannerNode (HRTF; coneInnerAngle 140, coneOuterAngle 300, coneOuterGain 0.5 ≈ for the exhaust's rearward directivity) → bus, plus a send to a shared reverb. `emitter.update(srcPos, srcFwd, listenerPose, dt)` sets `delay.delayTime.linearRampToValueAtTime(d/343, t+dt)`. Ramping the delay gives Doppler automatically; clamp the ramp slope to ±0.5 so a camera cut cannot wrap pitch, and on a cut (|Δd| > 30 m in one frame) jump with setValueAtTime under a 20 ms gain dip. Gain = min(1, 6/d) (chase ≈ 6 m as reference). Absorption: per-band ISO factor (see the rocket finding) or a lowpass at fc = 20000·(25/max(d,25))^0.8 (≈). Change the signatures to `gt3Sound.update(s, i, surface, view)` and `h2rSound.update(s, i, surface, view)`, with `view = { camera: state.camera, listener: camera, src: holder.position, heading: s.psi }`. When camera is 'driver', 'bonnet' or 'rider', bypass the emitter (dry, onboard chain). Set ctx.listener from camera.matrixWorld exactly as sound.js:208-214 does.

findings.title: Control messages at frame rate, smoothed once per block; instant on/off makes a click
findings.evidence: Smoothing runs once per 128-sample block (h2rSound.js:45-46, gt3Sound.js:61-63), so rpm is a staircase that follows the rAF rate. At 10 fps (as in headless runs or slow GPUs), a 3,000 rpm/s sweep moves in 300 rpm steps, about 5% or nearly a semitone at 6,000 rpm. `this.cut = this.tCut` and `* this.on` (h2rSound.js:108, gt3Sound.js:119) apply instantly. clicks.mjs: H2R crash (on 1→0 at 9,000 rpm WOT) makes a sample-to-sample jump of 0.766, against a steady-state maximum of 0.230. postMessage also allocates an object every frame on both threads.
findings.fix: Declare `static get parameterDescriptors() { return [{name:'rpm',defaultValue:900,automationRate:'a-rate'}, {name:'load'}, {name:'thr'}, {name:'cut'}, {name:'on'}, {name:'gearW'}, {name:'cabin'}]; }` and read `parameters.rpm[i]` (or [0] when its length is 1) inside the sample loop. On the main thread, `engine.parameters.get('rpm').setTargetAtTime(rpm, t, 0.015)`. Keep `on` ramped per sample: `this.onS += (on - this.onS) * (1 - Math.exp(-1/(sr*0.01)))`. Keep the discrete events (cut, shift edge, chirp) as messages.

findings.title: Pulse shape fixed in milliseconds instead of crank angle; level and brightness flattened by the final tanh and the compressor
findings.evidence: Pulse decay τ is 1.1–2.3 ms for the H2R (line 54) and 0.9–2.5 ms for the GT3 (line 73), independent of crank angle. At GT3 idle (22 ms firing interval) that is a sharp click train; the real blowdown lasts about 60–90° of crank (≈), i.e. 11–17 ms at 900 rpm and 1.1–1.7 ms at 9,000. Final shaping `Math.tanh(o*0.6*(0.8+1.6*(rpm/14000)^2))` (h2rSound.js:108; gt3Sound.js:119) followed by DynamicsCompressor(-12 dB, 3:1) flattens the dynamics. level.mjs, A-weighted at WOT: H2R +6.1/+9.2/+9.0/+10.1 dB at 6k/9k/12k/14k relative to 3k; GT3 +5.8/+7.9/+8.5/+11.1 dB at 4k/6k/8k/9k relative to 2k. Rule of thumb for exhaust orifice noise is about 30·log10(rpm ratio), i.e. +19 dB for H2R 3k→14k (estimate). Spectral centroid at WOT high rpm is 992 Hz (H2R 14k) and 675 Hz (GT3 8.5k), with energy above 5 kHz at -19 / -23 dB: dull for a 'shriek' (≈, by ear). DC offset 0.031 at the output (the DC blocker sits before the last tanh).
findings.fix: (1) Define the pulse in crank-angle space: a precomputed 256-entry table over 0–180° (≈ rise over 12°, exponential fall to 10% by 70°, then a low plateau for the displacement phase of the exhaust stroke), read with linear interpolation using `phi = theta - lastFiringTheta`. Let load make it narrower and higher (fold the table index by 1+0.4·load). (2) Add a load-dependent spectral tilt: a one-pole lowpass on the pulse with fc = 800 + 5000·load·(rpm/max) Hz (≈). (3) Replace the final tanh with a level curve `gain = 0.08 + 0.9·(rpm/max)^1.5` (≈ 30 dB/decade), and leave peak control to a single bus limiter (DynamicsCompressor threshold -3, ratio 20, knee 0). (4) Move the DC blocker to the very end.

findings.title: Exhaust modelled as fixed parallel band-pass filters: no pipe waveguide, temperature range too small, no intake/exhaust/mechanical separation
findings.evidence: h2rSound.js:32/48-50 uses 4 band-passes (170/480/1150/2600 Hz) with heat 1+0.12·rpm/14000+0.05·load. gt3Sound.js:36-37/66-68 uses two 4-filter banks 7% apart. The speed of sound in exhaust gas, c = 20.05·√T, goes from about 530 m/s (700 K, part load) to about 665 m/s (1100 K, WOT): +25%, against +17% modelled. The model has no harmonic comb of pipe modes and no reflected wave. The H2R intake is only white noise (line 104-105) with no induction pulses, although the ram-air duct and supercharger inlet sit in front of the rider. Everything is summed into one mono output, so exhaust (rear right on the H2R, central rear on the GT3), intake (H2R: front ram air; GT3: rear lid / plenum behind the seats) and mechanical sources cannot be placed or filtered separately per camera.
findings.fix: Per pipe, a digital waveguide: `y = x + R(z)·delay(y, N)`, with N = 2L/c·sr as a fractional delay (linear or allpass interpolation, ring buffer of 1024), R(z) = -0.85·onePoleLP(fc 3–5 kHz) at the open end (≈), and c taken from an EGT state that follows load with τ≈1.5 s. Estimated lengths (≈, mark as such): GT3, per bank 0.75 m headers plus 1.2 m to the silencer, followed by a Helmholtz silencer as one resonator at about 120 Hz with Q 1.5. H2R: 4-2-1 headers 0.6 m, collector 0.35 m, silencer about 150 Hz. Keep 2 of the current band-passes per bank as cabin/body formants. Reduce GT3 bank B detune from 7% to 2% (≈) so order 1.5 drops from about -7 to -8 dB to about -15 dB relative to order 3 (≈; measured now at 6k/8.5k WOT: -7.4/-8.3 dB). Change to `numberOfOutputs: 3` (exhaust, intake, mechanical) and route each to its own emitter (exhaust cone rearward, intake upward/forward).

findings.title: Supercharger whine synthesised at the shaft order (9.2x), not blade-pass; whine level not tied to boost physics
findings.evidence: h2rSound.js:95-97 uses sin(sc) and sin(2sc) at 9.2·fCrank, which is 2.15 kHz at 14,000 rpm. Published: 69 mm impeller, 6 blades at the tip expanding to 12 at the base, gear train 1.15 × 8 = 9.2× crank, about 130,000 /min (Kawasaki press kit). Blade-pass orders are therefore 55.2 (12.9 kHz at 14k, 5.5 kHz at 6k, 1.2 kHz at idle) and 110.4 (25.8 kHz at 14k, above Nyquist; it must not be synthesised as a plain sine). The planetary gear mesh tooth counts are not published.
findings.fix: Keep a weak shaft-order tone (imbalance, -20 dB) and add the 6-blade pass tone `sin(6·scPh)` with amplitude 0.004 + 0.05·boost (≈), plus its 2nd harmonic only while 12·fShaft < 0.45·sr: fade it with `gainNyq = clamp((0.45*sr - f)/(0.05*sr), 0, 1)` to avoid aliasing. Add slow amplitude and frequency jitter (±0.3%, 3–8 Hz random walk) so it whistles instead of beeping. Route it to the intake output (it radiates through the ram-air duct toward the rider). Mark everything as ≈ except the 9.2 ratio and the blade counts.

findings.title: Engine-state inputs: sound reads input throttle, not the throttle the engine gets; PDK blip and shift crack missing; GT3 order-12 tick is a sine
findings.evidence: gt3Car.js:313 blips the engine throttle during a downshift (`clamp((rpmWheel - s.rpm)/900,0,1)`), but gt3Sound.js:201-205 uses i.throttle, which is about 0 under braking. The blip is therefore heard as weak overrun pulses with pops, not a bark. On an upshift, load ×0.1 and cut=1 (lines 204-205) make the pulses 0.05/0.5 random, and no pop is injected, so there is no PDK crack. h2rSound.js:185 approximates traction control as a flat ×0.6 instead of reading the real cut (h2rBike.js:145). gt3Sound.js:113-114 renders the valve train as a pure order-12 sine (a whistle, not a tick). h2rSound.js:117/199 has a dead constant (`MAX`, `void MAX`).
findings.fix: Expose `s.engThr = thr` (gt3Car.js after line 321; h2rBike.js after line 147) and `s.Te = Te` (gt3Car.js:323; h2rBike.js after the Te line), and pass load = clamp(Te/fullTorque(rpm), 0, 1) and thr = s.engThr. Upshift edge (shift>0 && shiftDir>0, rising): over the next 40–80 ms set `pop = 1.2` once or twice and raise the pulse width (≈ ignition retard). Downshift: the blip is automatic once engThr is used. Valve train: a click train at order 12 (impulse → band-pass 4.5 kHz, Q 3, amplitude ∝ x9). Remove `MAX`.

findings.title: Wind and tyre layers: wrong speed law, frame-rate random squeal, gravel as low-passed hiss
findings.evidence: Wind gain is min(0.6,(speed/70)²·0.5) for the H2R (line 197) and (speed/80)²·0.35 for the GT3 (line 221): amplitude ∝ U², i.e. 40 dB/decade. SWOV helmet data, 94 dB → 106 dB from 100 → 160 km/h, is about 59 dB/decade (∝U³, dipole). Measured RMS: H2R wind 0.009 / 0.042 / 0.090 at 100 / 200 / 300 km/h, against engine RMS about 0.33–0.46 at WOT, so at 200 km/h wind sits about 18 dB under the engine where reality has it roughly equal or louder. Squeal frequency: `1150 + 180·sin(t·7.3) + 120·N.r()` re-randomised every frame (h2rSound.js:195; gt3Sound.js:219), so it jitters at frame rate. Gravel is noise low-passed at 260 Hz (no crunch). All layers loop the same 3 s noise buffer (h2rSound.js:127).
findings.fix: Wind: gain = k·(U/U0)³, capped. For the helmet (H2R rider camera) choose k so wind RMS roughly equals engine RMS at 100 km/h WOT in 4th gear (≈). Use two bands: a lowpass at 300 + 4·U Hz, and a band-pass around 1.5 kHz (turbulent buffeting) with 2–6 Hz amplitude modulation. For outside cameras, wind is the listener's own: keep it very low and make it independent of vehicle speed. Squeal: 2 band-passes at f and 2.03f, f random-walking at 0.5 Hz inside a worklet or via setTargetAtTime with a 0.3 s time constant; stick-slip AM at 25–40 Hz; f = 900 + 400·slipExcess (≈). Gravel: Poisson impulse train at rate ∝ speed·(0.5..1) into a band-pass at 2–5 kHz plus the existing rumble. Use separate 7–11 s noise buffers per layer.

findings.title: No cabin or helmet transfer beyond one lowpass; no reverb for the cars
findings.evidence: gt3Sound.js:146/213: inside = lowpass at 3.8 kHz (12 dB/oct), outside = 18 kHz. Missing: low-frequency cabin boom (modes about 40–100 Hz), mass-law mid attenuation, early reflections at about 2–4 ms (cabin about 1.3 m wide). The H2R has no helmet filter at all. There is no outdoor reverb: open flats with buildings would give a short late tail, while sound.js already builds a procedural 3.6 s impulse response.
findings.fix: In audioSpace.js, `makeIR(ctx, {seconds, t60, predelay, early:[[ms,gain]...], darken})`, generalised from sound.js:103-114 with a 50 ms cosine fade at the end. Outdoor: t60 1.2 s (τ = t60/6.91), predelay 25 ms, send -18 dB, wet level constant with distance (so the wet/dry ratio rises as the car recedes). Cabin chain: lowshelf +4 dB at 80 Hz → peaking -6 dB at 1.5 kHz, Q 0.8 → lowpass 2.8 kHz → convolver with a 60 ms IR (t60 0.12 s; early taps at 2.1/3.4/4.7 ms), 30% wet. Helmet (H2R rider): lowpass 2.5 kHz on the exhaust only (the intake is not filtered: it is in front), lowshelf +3 dB at 120 Hz (≈). All values ≈.

findings.title: Rocket: no Doppler, air absorption ~4x too bright, IR truncated at -34 dB, roar peak high compared with measured super-heavy spectra
findings.evidence: sound.js:226-253 uses retarded time th = t - d/c but no Doppler. dτ/dt = 1/(1+v_r/c) is about 0.41 for a booster leaving at 500 m/s, so the band filters should move about 1.3 octaves down. Air: fc = 15000·250/d (line 253) gives 15 kHz at 250 m, 3.75 kHz at 1 km and 375 Hz at 10 km. ISO 9613 at 20 °C / 70% RH (α dB/km: 125 Hz 0.4, 250 Hz 1.0, 500 Hz 1.9, 1 kHz 3.7, 2 kHz 9.7, 4 kHz 32.8, 8 kHz 117) puts the 3 dB point at about 2.5 kHz at 250 m, about 900 Hz at 1 km and about 110 Hz at 10 km. Reverb IR envelope exp(-(t-0.06)/0.9) truncated at 3.6 s, i.e. -34 dB (lines 103-113): an audible cut on the tail. The roar band-pass is 160 Hz with Q 0.5 (line 145), whereas measured SLS sound power peaks at 10–20 Hz at 1.4–1.8 km (Kellison & Gee 2023, JASA EL 3, 113601). The reverb send sits after the distance gain (line 136), so the wet level falls as 1/r too.
findings.fix: (1) Doppler: keep prevTh[i] and prevTc. `D = clamp((th - prevTh)/(tc - prevTc), 0.3, 2)` (only when live, not on seek). Multiply every band filter's base frequency and each loop's playbackRate (the shock train's rate) by D using setTargetAtTime with τ 0.1. Store base frequencies in src[i]. (2) Absorption: drop the single lowpass and apply per-band attenuation `10^(-α(fc)·d_km/20)` from the ISO table (log-interpolated) on each band gain: rumble fc 40, roar 160, tear 1100, crackle 2000, imp 1500. Keep one lowpass at the frequency where α·d = 6 dB for the residual top end. (3) IR: τ = 3.6/6.91 ≈ 0.52 s, or a 0.3 s cosine fade at the end. (4) Reverb send taken pre-distance (wet constant, dry 1/r). (5) Optional: move the 'roar' to about 60 Hz and add a soft-saturating bass enhancer (waveshaper on a 20–40 Hz band, then a 60–180 Hz band-pass) so the 10–20 Hz energy is perceived on small speakers. Mark ≈. (6) Booms: lowpass 2500 → 600–800 Hz to give a rise time of about 1–3 ms (≈).

findings.title: Architecture: three AudioContexts with three compressors; no automated DSP regression test
findings.evidence: Each module calls `new AC()` with its own DynamicsCompressor into destination (sound.js:66/98, gt3Sound.js:135/141, h2rSound.js:125/131). No tool in tools/ exercises the worklets: the only sound check is the context state in ux-check.mjs:275-284. Measured cost is about 0.8% of one core per worklet, so heavier DSP is affordable.
findings.fix: Create src/sim/audioBus.js with getAudio() → {ctx, bus, limiter, reverb, listener}: one lazily created context, a shared limiter and shared reverbs (outdoor and cabin). The three sound modules take their ctx from it. Add tools/sound-check.mjs to check:static, reusing the extraction from scratchpad/diag/run.mjs: `new Function('AudioWorkletProcessor','registerProcessor','sampleRate', src)`. Assertions: (a) deterministic inharmonic floor below -38 dB at H2R 14,000 and GT3 8,900 rpm; (b) chirp instantaneous frequency monotonically falling inside [800, 6000] Hz whatever the starting phase; (c) |DC| < 0.005; (d) max sample step at on 1→0 no larger than 1.2× the steady-state maximum; (e) A-weighted WOT level rise ≥ 15 dB from 3k to 14k (H2R) and from 2k to 9k (GT3) (≈ target); (f) no sinusoid above 0.45·sr; (g) render cost below 5% of one core.

plan:
Order of work: one commit per step. Run `npm run check:static` before each commit; run the full `npm run check` at the end of the block; update the README (in Spanish) with every change. Mark every new non-published number with ≈ in comments and in the README.

STEP 0 — Test harness first (tools/sound-check.mjs, added to check:static in package.json)
- Take the WORKLET template literal out of each sound file, as in scratchpad/diag/run.mjs (indexOf('const WORKLET = `') … '`;').
- Instantiate it with stub AudioWorkletProcessor and registerProcessor at sampleRate 48000, and render offline in 128-sample blocks.
- Implement the 7 assertions listed in the last finding; mark the not-yet-passing ones as expected failures until their step lands.
- The FFT, inharmonic-energy and A-weighting code in scratchpad/diag (analyse.mjs, variants.mjs, level.mjs) can be ported directly. Exclude bins below 30 Hz from the inharmonic total.

STEP 1 — Bug fixes, small and safe
- h2rSound.js
  - Fractional firing placement (code in finding 1).
  - Chirp on its own phase accumulator (finding 2).
  - Ramp `on` per sample (10 ms).
  - Move the DC blocker after the final shaper.
  - Remove MAX / `void MAX`.
- gt3Sound.js
  - Same fractional placement, per bank (this.cA, this.cB).
  - Same `on` ramp and DC-blocker move.
- h2rBike.js: expose `s.engThr` (after line 147) and `s.Te`.
- gt3Car.js: expose `s.engThr` (after line 321) and `s.Te` (after line 323).
- h2rSound.update: load = clamp(s.Te / engineTorque(rpm), 0, 1) (or engThr when not available); thr = s.engThr; add `shift: s.shift > 0 ? 1 : 0`. The chirp triggers on the shift's rising edge with load > 0.5 and rpm > 7000.
- gt3Sound.update: the same, using fullTorque.
- Verify with sound-check (a)–(d).

STEP 2 — AudioParam controls
- Add parameterDescriptors to both worklets for rpm, load, thr, cut, on, gearW, cabin.
- In process(), read the params per sample: `const P = (a, i) => a.length > 1 ? a[i] : a[0]`.
- Main thread: `node.parameters.get(k).setTargetAtTime(v, ctx.currentTime, 0.015)`.
- Keep postMessage only for events: shift edge, upshift crack.
- This removes the frame-rate staircase and the per-frame allocations.

STEP 3 — Shared audio infrastructure
- New src/sim/audioBus.js: one AudioContext, master → DynamicsCompressor limiter (-3 dB, ratio 20) → destination, plus outdoor and cabin reverbs from makeIR.
- New src/sim/audioSpace.js:
  - createEmitter(ctx, opts) chain: DelayNode(1.5 s) → air filter → ground-reflection DelayNode + gain → PannerNode (HRTF, with a cone) → bus, plus a reverb send.
  - emitter.update({ pos, fwd, listenerPos, dt }): delay ramp = Doppler, with cut detection; gain = min(1, dRef/d); ground-reflection path difference as in sound.js:247-251; ISO 9613 per-frequency absorption.
  - setListener(ctx, camera) (from sound.js:208-214).
  - makeIR(ctx, cfg) (from sound.js:103-114, with an end fade).
- Change sound.js, gt3Sound.js and h2rSound.js to take ctx from audioBus (keeping the opt-in click semantics and the visibility suspend).
- In sound.js, reuse makeIR and setListener.

STEP 4 — Camera-aware cars
- gt3Drive.js:562 → `sound.update(s, sim.input, s.surface[2], { camera: state.camera, cam: camera, pos: holder.position, psi: s.psi })`.
- h2rRide.js:330 → the same with `s.surface`.
- Inside the sound modules:
  - Onboard ('driver' / 'bonnet' / 'rider'): bypass the emitters. GT3 'driver' uses the cabin chain; H2R 'rider' uses the helmet chain.
  - Otherwise: exhaust emitter at the tailpipe (GT3 ≈ (-2.25, 0.45, 0) in car frame, cone facing rearward; H2R ≈ (-0.9, 0.55, +0.15)), intake emitter (GT3 rear lid ≈ (-1.6, 1.15, 0) facing up; H2R ram-air duct ≈ (+0.9, 0.6, 0) facing forward). Transform the positions with holder.matrixWorld.
- Requires numberOfOutputs: 3 in each worklet (exhaust, intake, mechanical) with outputChannelCount [1,1,1].
- Wind for outside cameras: low, independent of vehicle speed. Tyres and gravel go to an emitter at the contact patch.

STEP 5 — Timbre (worklets)
- (a) Crank-angle pulse table with load-dependent width (finding 5).
- (b) Load-dependent tilt lowpass.
- (c) Waveguide exhaust per pipe with EGT state and c = 20.05·√T (finding 6). Estimated lengths are ≈ and must be marked.
- (d) GT3 bank detune 7% → 2%. Target order 1.5 at about -15 dB relative to order 3 (≈), checked with analyse.mjs.
- (e) Replace the final tanh with a level curve ∝ (rpm/max)^1.5 plus the bus limiter. Target A-weighted rise ≥ 15 dB (≈).
- (f) Optional hybrid 'order layer': a 2D table of order gains over rpm × load (orders 0.5–24, every node marked ≈), synthesised as sin(k·theta) phase-locked to the same theta as the pulses so nothing beats. Bilinear crossfade between table nodes; each order faded to zero as k·f approaches 0.45·sr. Use it only to correct spectral balance, mixed at -12 dB under the pulse path.
- (g) ADAA on tanh, low priority: measured aliasing floor is about -44 to -48 dB. y = (logcosh(x_n) - logcosh(x_{n-1})) / (x_n - x_{n-1}), falling back to tanh((x_n + x_{n-1})/2) when |Δx| < 1e-5.

STEP 6 — Vehicle-specific sources
- H2R
  - Blade-pass whine at 55.2× crank, plus its 110.4× harmonic only below 0.45·sr, routed to the intake output.
  - Keep the 9.2× shaft tone at -20 dB.
  - Relief-valve chirp: tone plus 3–5 kHz noise.
  - Chain mesh tone: front sprocket of 18 teeth. f = (wR·42/18)/(2π)·18 Hz from s.wR (rear wheel), i.e. rear rev/s × 42 (published 42/18). Amplitude ≈ 0.006·speed-dependent.
  - Induction pulses through an airbox resonator (≈ 400 Hz, Q 4) feeding the intake output.
- GT3
  - On the upshift edge: 1–2 pops plus a widened pulse (≈ 60 ms).
  - Order-12 click train instead of the sine.
  - PDK gear mesh: input-shaft order × engaged-gear tooth count is not published, so keep the existing final-drive pinion whine marked ≈.
- Both: wind ∝ U³ with two bands and buffeting AM; squeal as 2 random-walk band-passes with stick-slip AM; gravel as Poisson impulses; separate noise buffers.

STEP 7 — Rocket (sound.js)
- Doppler from dτ/dt applied to band filter frequencies and loop playbackRates. Store base frequencies; skip on seek (|Δth| > 3 s already guarded at line 257).
- ISO 9613 per-band absorption replacing line 253 (and line 259 for one-shots).
- IR fade (or τ = 0.52 s).
- Reverb send taken before the distance gain.
- Boom lowpass about 700 Hz (≈).
- Optional bass enhancer for the 10–20 Hz region.

STEP 8 — Validation
- Extend tools/sound-check.mjs with:
  - a Doppler unit test: emitter passing at 69 m/s and 14 m; the received pitch ratio between approach and recession must be 1.50 ± 0.03, measured via autocorrelation on an OfflineAudioContext-free Node simulation of the delay-line formula;
  - an absorption test against the ISO table values;
  - a chirp test.
- Listen in the browser with frames.mjs plus manual audio. Do not regenerate the screenshot gallery.
- Update the README sections (GT3 sound around README.md:911, H2R around 811, launch sound around 1174) in Spanish, describing the new model and listing which numbers are published and which are ≈.
